$ hemma doctor --help
exit: 0
--- stdout ---
--- stderr ---
hemma doctor — audit the repo (gitignore, Caddyfile imports, drift, auth,
deploy readiness)

Usage: hemma doctor [--fix | --json]

Flags:
  -f, --fix   Apply fixes: reconcile generated files and .gitignore entries.
      --json  Print the findings as JSON and change nothing (the web UI runs it
              over ssh to audit the other hosts; cannot be combined with --fix).

doctor audits THIS host's checkout only; the web UI's Issues page covers every host.

On a host that serves sites it also checks that what changed on disk has been
deployed: one advisory for the auth snippet, and one for each service that has
extra directives, each saying whether the running proxy matches what is on disk.
They never affect the exit code; the fix is 'hemma apply' on that host, or
'hemma deploy'.

The auth checks are read-only advisories (hemma never writes the provider's
config, users database, or compose file); --fix cannot resolve them. Each
advisory prints a headline (the consequence), the mechanism, and a fixed
'fix:'/'then:' grammar — the exact edit to paste in (e.g. the
X_AUTHELIA_CONFIG value that wires the generated access-control file into
the auth container) and the follow-up command (usually 'hemma apply').

There is no separate public-horizon check: hemma is the sole author of each
host's cloudflared config.yml (generated from every service's 'public' field,
same as the DNS/Caddy files), so a 'public: true' service with no matching
config.yml entry — e.g. because defaults.tunnel-dir isn't set — surfaces as
ordinary generated-file drift, the same as any other missing/orphaned file.

The deploy-readiness check verifies each remote deploy target has a host key
in THIS machine's known_hosts ('ssh-keygen -F' against the host's ip and its
ssh destination — either counts). 'hemma deploy' sshes with BatchMode=yes,
which cannot answer the first-connection trust prompt, so a missing entry
fails deploy outright. Not --fix-able (hemma does not own known_hosts): the
recipe is to connect once interactively and verify the fingerprint. doctor
never connects anywhere — whether ssh auth actually WORKS is verified by
deploy itself, in its phase-0 probe.
